title: A 1% Fee Doesn't Take 1% of Your Money

beats.text: A one percent fee sounds tiny.
It's not. Over forty years, it can take almost a third of your money.
Say you invest ten thousand dollars, and it grows seven percent a year.
After forty years, you have about a hundred and fifty thousand.
Now take one percent off, every single year. You're growing at six.
Forty years later? About a hundred and three thousand.
The fee didn't take one percent. It took forty-seven thousand dollars.
Because a fee doesn't just take your money. It takes everything that money would have earned.
And a two percent fee? It takes more than half.
So next time someone tells you it's only one percent,
